html:
The Syrian civil war was the war in Syria that began with protests against the government of Bashar al-Assad in March 2011 and ended when rebels took Damascus in December 2024. It was one of the deadliest wars of the 21st century.

The protests were part of the Arab Spring. The government answered with gunfire and mass arrests, soldiers deserted, and by 2012 the country was at war. It soon split into many fronts:

  • the government, backed by Iran, Hezbollah and, from 2015, the Russian air force;
  • many rebel groups, from secular to Islamist, backed at times by Turkey, Gulf states and the West;
  • the Islamic State, which declared a caliphate in 2014 from its base at Raqqa;
  • Kurdish-led forces in the north east, who fought the Islamic State with American air support.

The war destroyed much of Aleppo, Homs and other cities, and damaged old sites such as the norias of Hama. In 2015 the Islamic State blew up the Temple of Bel at Palmyra. Hundreds of thousands of people were killed, and about half the population fled their homes. Millions went abroad, mainly to Turkey, Lebanon and Jordan, in the Syrian refugee crisis, and in 2015 many reached Europe, driving the European migrant crisis.

By 2020 the front lines had frozen. The earthquakes of February 2023 hit the worn-out north hard. In late 2024 a rebel offensive from Idlib swept south in less than two weeks, and Assad fled to Russia.
sum: The Syrian civil war was the war in Syria that began with protests against the government of Bashar al-Assad in March 2011 and ended when rebels took Damascus in December 2024. It was one of the deadliest wars of the 21st century.
